title: The Government Filed a Brief for the Algorithm: How the DOJ Killed America's First AI Antidiscrimination Law
rationale: In April 2026, the Trump DOJ sided with Elon Musk's xAI to challenge Colorado's SB24-205 — a first-of-its-kind state law requiring AI systems used in hiring, mortgage lending, and student admissions to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination based on race, gender, age, and income. Enforcement was suspended on April 27, right before its June 30 implementation deadline. The DOJ's argument: requiring companies to prevent discrimination violates the Fourteenth Amendment's equal protection clause; xAI's: labeling their outputs 'discriminatory' violates their First Amendment right to 'pursue truth.' This is corporate capture at its most naked — the nation's chief law enforcement agency in court as Big Tech's co-counsel — and the question Dawn demands answered is the one no regulator will touch: if the DOJ is now xAI's lawyer, who's left to protect the people the algorithm harms?

sources.name: DOJ Press Release: Justice Department Intervenes in xAI Lawsuit Challenging Colorado's 'Algorithmic Discrimination' Law
Colorado Sun: Justice Department joins Elon Musk's xAI in effort to block Colorado AI antidiscrimination law
Norton Rose Fulbright: xAI sues, DOJ intervenes, enforcement of Colorado's AI Act suspended

title: The Robot Beside You: What Humanoid Machines Actually Do on the Factory Floor in 2026
rationale: Figure 02 at BMW's Spartanburg plant, Digit inside Amazon fulfillment centers, Atlas at Hyundai's Georgia facility, and Apollo on Mercedes-Benz assembly lines mark 2026 as the year humanoid robots crossed from demo to deployment — and the real story is the gap between Hollywood's vision and the precise, narrow material-handling jobs these machines actually perform. Kenji's 'explain the mechanism' mandate fits perfectly: why bipedal form matters in human-designed spaces, what ±2mm repeatability means versus ±0.02mm for fixed arms, how AI perception/navigation enables the flexibility trade-off, and what it looks like for a human worker to take a shift alongside a robot colleague.
